headline: High-risk shared-write pair: Devin and Plandex both have broad shell, filesystem, git, and network access, creating dangerous prompt-injection, data-leakage, and cascading-error pathways by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin can use MCP, browsers, and shared integrations, while Plandex reads/writes project files and stdin/stdout. A prompt-injection path exists if Devin’s outputs are copied into Plandex plans or shared files, but no direct shared channel is documented between them. The risk is real yet not inherently automatic.
conditions: IF Devin writes attacker-controlled instructions into a shared repo file or Slack thread that Plandex later ingests
IF Plandex auto-applies content originating from Devin without human review
mitigations: Disable auto-apply in Plandex for any content sourced from Devin
Require manual review of Devin-generated files before Plandex reads them
Keep Devin and Plandex on separate workspaces/repos
Use a provenance note in shared files identifying agent-authored content
requires-engineering: add content provenance checks between the agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch source code and have broad filesystem access; Devin additionally handles issue trackers, team chat, docs, and integration tokens, while Plandex can send data to a model provider. If they share a workspace or repo, sensitive code or tokens can flow from Devin into Plandex’s inference path. The blast radius includes multiple work products and secrets.
conditions: IF Devin and Plandex operate on the same repository checkout or cloud workspace
IF Devin places secrets or internal chat content into files that Plandex reads
IF Plandex forwards those files to its model provider
mitigations: Separate repositories and workspaces for the two agents
Do not place secrets in files accessible to Plandex
Restrict Plandex to non-sensitive branches only
Rotate any exposed integration tokens immediately
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can execute shell commands, write the filesystem, and modify git state. Devin’s shared-state integrations and Plandex’s plan-local sandbox do not guarantee locking across the same repo, so concurrent edits can overwrite each other or corrupt git state. This is a default-dangerous overlap with potentially irreversible repository damage.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same git repository or working tree
IF edits are made concurrently without an external lock
IF either agent auto-commits or auto-applies changes
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate branch
Serialize write access with a manual lock
Disable auto-commit and auto-apply
Review diffs before merge
requires-engineering: add repo-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin can autonomously act inside its workspace and Plandex can stage-and-apply changes after planning. If Plandex consumes Devin-produced code or instructions as authoritative, errors can cascade from one agent’s output into the other’s applied changes. The pair lacks a documented verification boundary, so the safer assumption is high risk.
conditions: IF Plandex uses Devin-generated artifacts as inputs to its plan without independent verification
IF Devin’s outputs are converted into commits or applied patches by Plandex
IF either agent is allowed to act on the other’s output without a human review step
mitigations: Require human verification between agents
Use a checklist for any agent-to-agent handoff
Limit Plandex to drafting only when fed Devin output
Limit Devin to analysis only when feeding Plandex
requires-engineering: add automated validation gates

E_compliance.rationale: Devin touches issue trackers, team chat, docs, and secrets, while Plandex touches source code and can transmit content to a model provider. If regulated or confidential data is present in Devin’s broader data classes and then moved into Plandex’s external inference path, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific regime, so medium is the prudent choice.
conditions: IF regulated data from issue trackers, chat, or docs is copied into Plandex inputs
IF the model provider or Plandex Cloud retains that data longer than Devin’s workspace policy
IF the deployment is subject to a residency or retention requirement
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of Plandex inputs
Use self-hosted Plandex where possible
Minimize logging of shared artifacts
Review retention settings for both tools
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies
